main_text.p: totum, fed pars duntaxat. Itaque doctrinæ capax non adæquat vocabulum homo: fed cō-iunctè definitur Animal doctrinæ capax. Sic rectè dicetur: Si fol lucet, dies eft. Si dies eft, fol lucet. Sed non natura Enuntiationis reci-procantis illa eft, verū argumentatio ex cauf-fis & effectis. Et quamuis urgeri pofsit, hæc inter fe conuerti: Vt lux folis, eft dies: fic dies eft lux folis: tamen perspicuum eft, hanc effe definitionem, & definitum: fed eam non verā & folidam, fed ex caufsis & effectis adumbra-tam: de quarum vtraque nunc eft differen-di locus.
main_text.head: CAP. XIIII.
main_text.p: Q[?]VONIAM igitur de priore Enuntiationum genere fatis dixisti, deinceps de ea dicamus, quam principem & Reginam omnium superiùs appellasti.

Quid eft Definitio? Oratio (inquit Cicero) quæ id quod definitur explicat quid fit. Et alibi, Oratio quæ quid fit id de quo agitur explicat quàmbreuissimè. Item, Oratio quæ complicatam animi notionem euoluit. Item, quæ inuolutæ rei notionem aperit. Item, quæ quasi inuolutum euoluit, id de quo quæritur. Item, quæ inuolutam animi notionem explicat. Ité, eft quasi patefactio rerum opertarū,

page.notes: No printed marginal notes. The woodcut initial at the start of the chapter is decorative; its letter is read as Q with a doubt, marked [?]. Long s is printed as s throughout (e.g. "pofsit", "caufsis", "fatis"), and these are kept as printed. "Vt" and "vrgeri" are changed to ut and urgeri per the u/v rule; "Ité" is kept as printed. Light stains and show-through at the edges of the page are not transcribed.
